messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations can lead to a $50 fine and points on the license. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs require a full stop before proceeding. | Failure to yield can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **School Bus Rules** | • When a school bus stops and its red lights flash, all vehicles must stop.
• In Texas, this applies to all directions of traffic. | Violations can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | Improper lane changes can result in a $50 fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• No parking in front of a driveway or in a fire lane.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Violations can lead to towing. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running a red light is a $50 fine.
• Failing to stop at a stop sign is a $50 fine. | Points may be added to the driver’s record. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense (e.g., DUI = 4 points). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain insurance can result in license suspension. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial vehicles must display a valid commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Trucks over 10,000 lb must have a valid CDL. | Violations can lead to fines and license revocation. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergency** | • Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) provides roadside assistance for registered vehicles.
• In emergencies, call 911. | Emergency services are free for residents. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed limit signs**: Always obey posted signs; they override default limits. - **Seat belt**: Mandatory for all occupants. - **Cell phone**: Hands‑free only. - **DUI**: Zero tolerance for under‑21 drivers. - **School bus**: Stop in all directions. - **Parking**: No parking near crosswalks or in fire lanes. ### Where to Find More Information - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** – State statutes governing traffic laws. - **Local County Courts** – For specific citations and penalties. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular rule or how to handle a specific traffic situation!
